name: Networked Social Product Foundation
userOutcome: An existing or new user can deliberately opt into a networked identity and later participate in private group predictions without silent migration, false lock confirmation, cross-environment data leakage, or loss of local history.
entryPoints: Network, sync, privacy, and account recovery states
productionDataSource: Hybrid authority: local SwiftData for drafts and legacy private journal data until consent; a selected versioned backend for accounts, relationships, groups, social forecasts, server timestamps, resolutions, scores, moderation, and audit. The backend provider is not selected until F0.3.
errorBehavior: Drafts and legacy records remain recoverable after authentication, migration, sync, or network failure. Social records display queued or failed states until server acknowledgement; the app never reports a forecast as locked, a resolution as final, or a score as changed before authoritative persistence. Retry is idempotent and never attaches queued work to a different account.
layoutScenarios: iPad portrait and landscape where supported
accessibilityRequirements: Account, visibility, migration, invite, forecast, lock, error, retry, and recovery state is exposed as text to VoiceOver.
No status or confidence meaning relies only on color, motion, chart geometry, or haptics.
Primary capture and response controls have logical focus order and at least 44 by 44 point targets.
Reduced Motion provides an informationally equivalent static lock and reveal state.
prohibitedBehavior: Do not upload existing journal content without explicit migration consent.
Do not claim a social forecast is locked before server acknowledgement.
Do not use client time as the authoritative social deadline or timestamp.
Do not authorize access only by hiding client controls; enforce every visibility and role rule server-side.
Do not log prediction text, private notes, invite tokens, authentication material, precise location, or private group names.
Do not introduce a backend vendor SDK or third-party runtime dependency before F0.3 and DEC-007 are satisfied.
Do not enable Social v2 from UserDefaults, process arguments, an environment/account mismatch, an unsupported contract/build, or an invalid feature dependency graph.
Do not mix subjective private-group results into verified public rankings.
Do not use fake identities, fabricated resolver evidence, or undisclosed production sample data.
acceptanceTests: The approved backend spike rejects forged or replayed Sign in with Apple identity and unauthorized group access.
Atomic lock tests reject late, duplicate, stale, removed-member, and cross-account submissions.
Migration fixture tests prove zero record loss, no pre-consent network upload, interruption recovery, and idempotent retry.
Environment tests prove development credentials and data cannot access QA or production.
Telemetry and push payload tests prove prohibited content is absent.
Typed API contract and generated client fixtures agree on state, error, pagination, and idempotency behavior.
Every Social v2 client flag is disabled by default and fails closed when its environment, account, contract, build, or dependency precondition does not match.
VoiceOver, largest Dynamic Type, dark mode, Reduce Motion, relaunch, offline, and physical-device evidence exists before the Phase 1 QA promotion.
